name: VARK Learning Styles Questionnaire
instructions: Choose the answer which best explains your preference.
The questionnaire says more than one answer may be selected if a single answer does not match your perception.
Question 15 in the supplied PDF is an instruction: “Ignore question 1.” It is not a question with answer options.

items.prompt: How many syllables are in your first name?

options.text: one
two
three
more than three

items.prompt: You are about to give directions to a person who is standing with you. They are staying in a hotel in town and want to visit your house later. They have a rental car. You would:

options.text: draw a map on paper
tell them the directions
write down the directions (without a map)
collect them from the hotel in my car

items.prompt: You are not sure whether a word should be spelled ‘dependent’ or ‘dependant’. I would:

options.text: look it up in the dictionary
see the word in my mind and choose the way it looks
sound it out in my mind
write both versions down on paper and choose one

items.prompt: You have just received the latest copy of a magazine with an itinerary for a conference, this is of interest to someone else. You would:

options.text: phone them immediately
send them a copy of the printed itinerary
show them on a map of the world
share what I plan to do at each place I visit

items.prompt: You are going to cook something as a special treat for your family. You would:

options.text: cook something familiar without the need for instructions
thumb through the cookbook looking for ideas from the pictures
refer to a specific cookbook where there is a good recipe

items.prompt: A group of students from another school has been assigned to you to find out about the geology of your local area. You would:

options.text: drive them to a wildlife reserve or park
show them slides and photographs
give them pamphlets or a book on wildlife reserves or parks
give them a talk on wildlife reserves or parks

items.prompt: You are about to purchase a new compass clinometer. Other than price, what would most influence your decision?

options.text: the salesperson telling you what you want to know
reading the details about it in a journal
playing with the controls and listening to it (road testing it)
it looks really smart and fashionable

items.prompt: Recall a time in your life when you learned how to do something like playing a new board game. Try to avoid choosing a very physical skill, eg. riding a bike. You learned best by:

options.text: visual clues – pictures, diagrams, charts
written instructions
listening to somebody explaining it
doing it or trying it

items.prompt: You have an eye problem. You would prefer the doctor to:

options.text: tell me what is wrong
show me a diagram of what is wrong
use a model to show what is wrong

items.prompt: You are about to learn to use a new program on a computer. You would:

options.text: sit down at the keyboard and begin to experiment with the program features
read the manual which comes with the program
telephone a friend and ask questions about it

items.prompt: You are staying in a hotel and have a rental car. You would like to visit friends whose address/location you do not know. You would like them to:

options.text: draw a map on paper
tell directions
write down the directions (without a map)
collect me from the hotel in their car

items.prompt: Apart from the price, what would most influence your decision to buy a particular textbook?

options.text: I have used a copy before
a friend talking about it
quickly reading parts of it
the way it looks is appealing

items.prompt: A new movie has arrived in town. What would most influence your decision to go (or not go)?

options.text: I heard a radio review of it
I read a review of it
I saw a preview of it

items.prompt: Do you prefer a lecturer who likes to use:

options.text: a textbook, handouts, readings
flow diagrams, charts, graphs
field trips, labs, practical sessions
discussion, guest speakers
